sponsored.t: Authorizes a person to limit the gambling self-exclusion to online platforms
sponsored.ls: Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law
sponsored.sum: Authorizes a person to limit the gambling self-exclusion to online platforms.

sponsored.t: Enacts the "Count me out!: Ending New York funding of designated foreign terrorist organizations act"
sponsored.sum: Enacts the "Count me out!: Ending New York funding of designated foreign terrorist organizations act" to prohibit not-for-profit corporations from knowingly providing material support or resources to designated foreign terrorist organizations; allows for recovery of a civil penalty by the state attorney general; creates a private right of action for violations.

sponsored.t: Allows certain persons to practice as a mental health practitioner under supervision for a certain period of time if application and fee requirements are met
sponsored.sum: Provides that a person with a master's level degree required for practicing as a mental health practitioner shall be allowed to practice under supervision for a period of up to ninety days after the submission of the required application and fees.

sponsored.t: Authorizes the division of housing and community renewal to enforce building codes
sponsored.sum: Authorizes the division of housing and community renewal to enforce building codes for properties owned by local municipalities and housing authorities.

sponsored.t: Enacts the "licensure incentives and fee-support for testing (LIFT) act"
sponsored.sum: Enacts the "licensure incentives and fee-support for testing (LIFT) act"; establishes the social work licensure examination voucher program to provide low-income individuals vouchers to cover the cost of the examination, regardless of the number of examination attempts, required for licensure as a licensed master social worker or licensed clinical social worker.

sponsored.t: Establishes the crime of private carrier package theft
sponsored.sum: Establishes the crime of private carrier package theft; designates private carrier package theft a class E felony punishable by a fine of not more than two hundred fifty thousand dollars.

sponsored.t: Allows the city of New York to convey certain lands to the Amity Little League, Inc.
sponsored.sum: Allows the city of New York to convey the Amity Little League Baseball Complex to the Amity Little League, Inc. for a period of forty years; subjects the conveyance to the provisions of the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure.

sponsored.t: Provides dormitory authority financing for construction of buildings to be used as a school for Yeshiva Ohr Yoseph
sponsored.sum: Provides dormitory authority financing for construction of buildings to be used as a school for Yeshiva Ohr Yoseph.

sponsored.t: Relates to certain procedural protections granted to third-party sellers and seller profiles of online marketplaces
sponsored.sum: Relates to certain procedural protections granted to third-party sellers and seller profiles of online marketplaces; provides that online marketplaces must provide notice and an opportunity to respond before a seller or profile is suspended; provides that a suspended third-party seller or seller profile shall have the right to appeal the determination of the online marketplace in seeking account reinstatement.

sponsored.t: Requires health insurance plans to provide coverage for continuous blood glucose monitors for all children
sponsored.sum: Requires health insurance plans to provide coverage for continuous blood glucose monitors for all children; requires coverage for glucose monitoring devices for all sugar disorders.

sponsored.t: Relates to the handling of certain unclaimed human remains
sponsored.sum: Prohibits unclaimed human remains from being buried, cremated, or otherwise finally disposed of unless such remains have first been entered into the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System, and for a period of time thereafter as specified by the commissioner of health.
sponsored.fis: Potential cost savings to local governments where burial expenses are assumed by private religious organizations.

sponsored.t: Relates to newborn screening for Gaucher disease
sponsored.sum: Requires that newborns are tested for Gaucher disease.

sponsored.t: Requires certain manufacturers to sell and distribute plastic beverage containers with tethered plastic beverage caps
sponsored.sum: Requires manufacturers with gross annual beverage sale revenues of ten million dollars or more, beginning January 1, 2030, to sell and distribute plastic beverage containers with tethered plastic beverage caps or openings from which the beverage can be consumed while the plastic beverage cap remains screwed onto or otherwise affixed to the plastic beverage container; requires manufacturers with gross annual beverage sale revenues of one million dollars or more to comply by January 1, 2033.

sponsored.t: Relates to reimbursement for nonpublic school safety equipment grants
sponsored.sum: Provides that reimbursement payable for grants for nonpublic school safety equipment shall be paid within twelve months of the nonpublic school furnishing all required application materials for such grant to the department of education; requires the commissioner of education to report on any such reimbursements payable.

sponsored.t: Relates to providing transportation after four o'clock
sponsored.sum: Relates to providing transportation after four o'clock.

sponsored.t: Prohibits certain surcharges on credit or debit card transactions
sponsored.sum: Prohibits certain surcharges on certain credit or debit card transactions in the city of New York; provides that no agency or department of the city of New York, or any tribunal located therein, shall be authorized to impose a surcharge on a holder who elects to use a credit or debit card in lieu of payment by cash, check, or similar means to pay any fine, civil penalty, or fee owed.

sponsored.t: Relates to school bus transportation
sponsored.sum: Provides that school bus transportation be provided where: a parent or guardian of a child not residing in the district on the April first date submits a written request within thirty days after establishing residence in the district; a family moves to a different dwelling within the district during the school year; a school moves locations from one location to another; or a parent or guardian chooses a nonpublic school for their child after April first.

sponsored.t: Requires a payroll services business to compile and provide annual wage and tax statements and/or year-end forms to clients
sponsored.sum: Requires a payroll services business to compile and provide annual wage and tax statements and/or year-end forms to clients without additional cost or delay.

sponsored.t: Waives the biennial attorney registration fee for New York attorneys who are employed in a public service job
sponsored.sum: Waives the biennial attorney registration fee for New York attorneys who are employed in a public service job.

sponsored.t: Relates to extending the duration of limited permits to practice licensed clinical social work and licensed master social work
sponsored.sum: Extends the duration of limited permits to practice licensed clinical social work and use the title licensed clinical social worker, or practice licensed master social work and use the title licensed master social worker from twelve to twenty-four months with the ability to be renewed for up to two additional one-year periods.

sponsored.t: Relates to transitional care placements by the office for people with developmental disabilities
sponsored.sum: Provides that an adult individual who has transferred into the OPWDD system of care from a transitional care placement at an out-of-state or in-state residential school or adult program associated with a residential school, and whose health, safety, or welfare are being adversely affected in the OPWDD system of care, is allowed to return to their prior transitional care placement, funded by OPWDD, under certain conditions.

sponsored.t: Relates to the registration of bicycles with electric assist used for commercial purposes
sponsored.sum: Requires the registration of bicycles with electric assist used for commercial purposes; provides liability of employers for certain violations.

sponsored.t: Includes the attacks on September 11, 2001 in courses of instruction in patriotism and citizenship
sponsored.sum: Includes the attacks on September 11, 2001 in courses of instruction in patriotism and citizenship.

sponsored.t: Prohibits the use of state aid by colleges and universities to fund or provide membership in academic institutions that are boycotting a country or higher education institutions of a country
sponsored.sum: Prohibits the use of state aid by colleges and universities to fund or provide membership in academic institutions that are boycotting a country or higher education institutions of a country.

sponsored.t: Requires epinephrine auto-injector devices at children's overnight, summer day and traveling summer camps
sponsored.sum: Requires epinephrine devices at children's overnight, summer day and traveling summer day camps.

sponsored.t: Authorizes the presence of epinephrine auto-injector devices on pre-school premises
sponsored.sum: Authorizes the presence of epinephrine auto-injector devices on pre-school premises.

sponsored.t: Requires all persons in a city having a population of one million or more operating a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter to wear a helmet
sponsored.sum: Requires all persons in a city having a population of one million or more operating a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter to wear a helmet; imposes a civil penalty for violation of such requirement.

sponsored.t: Enacts the "Give Kids a Chance - Carter and Ray's Law"; mandates health insurance coverage for congenital anomalies
sponsored.sum: Enacts the "Give Kids a Chance - Carter and Ray's Law" mandating health insurance coverage for congenital anomalies including certain reconstructive services, habilitative services, and inpatient and outpatient services.

sponsored.t: Enhances criminal penalties for criminal mischief and larceny offenses committed at a place of religious worship
sponsored.sum: Enhances criminal penalties for criminal mischief and larceny offenses committed at a place of religious worship and for cemetery desecration.

sponsored.t: Increases the mandatory retirement age of members of the uniformed force of the fire department of the city of New York from sixty-five to sixty-seven
sponsored.sum: Increases the mandatory retirement age of members of the uniformed force of the fire department of the city of New York from sixty-five to sixty-seven.

sponsored.t: Prohibits the issuance of tickets to residential occupants for certain violations of the sanitation code
sponsored.sum: Prohibits the issuance of violations or tickets during certain weekend hours to residential occupants for violations of the sanitation department regulations regarding placing trash or garbage out for collection earlier than allowed under the city routing system designated hours.

sponsored.t: Enacts the "building retention and internship-to-degree graduate employment (BRIDGE) act"
sponsored.sum: Enacts the "building retention and internship-to-degree graduate employment (BRIDGE) act"; provides limited work permits for students in a master of social work program; establishes policies and procedures for such work permit.

sponsored.t: Directs the department of health to establish an alternative payment methodology (APM) for Federally Qualified Health Centers to preserve and improve patient access to fertility care
sponsored.sum: Directs the department of health to establish an alternative payment methodology (APM) for federally qualified health centers to preserve and improve patient access to fertility care.
sponsored.fis: None. Any supplemental payment is part of the already approved state plan amendment that the State allocated the funds in previous years as part of a 90-10% federal state match.

sponsored.t: Relates to certain crimes of interference with health care services or religious worship
sponsored.sum: Relates to certain crimes of interference with health care services or access to places of religious worship; expands interference to include groups of two or more people demonstrating or preparing to demonstrate twenty-five feet outside of reproductive health care facilities and places of religious worship.

sponsored.t: Prohibits the issuance of tickets to residential occupants for certain violations of the sanitation code
sponsored.sum: Prohibits the issuance of violations or tickets during certain weekend hours to residential occupants for violations of the sanitation department regulations regarding placing trash or garbage out for collection earlier than allowed under the city routing system designated hours.

appr.text: APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 81 Chapter 705 MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 8256, entitled: "AN ACT to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the issuance of tickets to residential occupants for certain violations of the sanitation code" APPROVED The bill would allow for changes related to times for setting out of refuse and recycling within the City of New York. The intent of this bill was to ensure that rules regarding set out times do not disrupt New York City residents' religious observations. While I support the intent of the bill, it raised several issues related to its practical administration. sponsored.t: Relates to ensuring continued access to backup devices for patients with cochlear implants
sponsored.sum: Requires insurance coverage to backup devices for patients with cochlear implants during the initial implantation and for replacements and upgrades.
sponsored.fis: Minimal. While insurance providers may incur additional costs for cover- ing backup devices, the overall impact is expected to be limited. The potential long-term savings from avoiding complications related to interrupted hearing may offset initial expenses.

veto.text: VETO MESSAGE - No. 99 TO THE SENATE: I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill: Senate Bill Number 8265-A, entitled: "AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to ensuring contin- ued access to backup devices for patients with cochlear implants" NOT APPROVED This bill would require large group health insurance policies to provide coverage for a backup set of the external components of a cochlear implant device to ensure that patients with cochlear implants have continuous use of such devices. Cochlear implants are important devices for individuals with severe hearing loss that can significantly improve one's ability to understand speech and perceive sounds, and I support the goal of the bill, which is to expand access to such devices. However, large group health insurance policies are not currently required to cover cochlear implants. As such, the bill would…
